The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 58, verse 1:

It was a custom of the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic age of ignorance) that when a man became angry with his wife for some reason, he would say to her, "You are to me as my mother's back" (ظہار, zihar). By this phrase the woman was not divorced, nor could the husband have marital relations with her. Thus this woman remained suspended forever. Besides other oppressions, this was one oppression to which a woman in the age of Jahiliyyah was subjected.

When Islam appeared, the first incident of zihar to occur in Islamic society is the one to which this verse refers. The Islamic law of zihar had not yet been enforced. Imam Ahmad narrates from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim and Ya'qub, both from Abi, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Ma'mar ibn Abdullah ibn Hanzalah, from Yusuf ibn Abdullah ibn Salam, from Khuwaylah bint Tha'labah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "By Allah, the opening verses of Surah al-Mujadilah were revealed concerning me and Aws ibn al-Samit. I was his wife. He was very old and of bad temper. One day he came to me and I argued with him over some matter. He became very angry and said to me, 'You are to me as the back of my mother.' After this he went away and stayed for some time in a gathering of people, then he returned. I saw that he wished to have marital relations with me. I said, 'By Allah, in whose hand is the soul of Khuwaylah, you shall not come near me. You have said what you have said. Now this matter will go to the Messenger of Allah, and until Allah and His Messenger issue a command, you shall not come near me.' He attacked me, and I restrained him as a woman restrains an old man. In short, I pushed him away from me. After this I went to some of my neighbours and asked them for clothes on loan. Then I reached the Messenger of Allah. I sat before him and related the whole matter to him, and I complained of her husband's bad conduct. The Messenger of Allah said, 'He is your paternal cousin, an old man; fear Allah concerning him.' By Allah, I kept insisting until the Qur'an was revealed. The Messenger of Allah was immediately overtaken by a state which did not usually come upon him. After this state left him, he said to me, 'Khuwaylah, Allah has revealed the Qur'an concerning you and your husband.' Then he recited these verses to me:"

﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your dialogue. Indeed Allah is Hearing and Seeing. Those among you who divorce their wives by zihar — their wives are not their mothers; their mothers are only those who gave birth to them. And indeed they utter an evil word and a falsehood. And indeed Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving. And those who divorce their wives by zihar and then wish to retract what they said — then the freeing of a slave before they touch one another. That is what you are admonished to do, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do. And whoever does not find (a slave) — then fasting for two months consecutively before they touch one another. And whoever is unable — then feeding sixty needy persons. That is so that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger. These are the limits of Allah, and for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.﴾

She said: The Messenger of Allah told me to instruct him to free a slave. I said, "What does he have that he could free a slave?" He said, "Then let him fast two consecutive months." I said, "By Allah, he is an old man; he cannot fast two consecutive months." He said, "Then let him feed sixty needy persons, a wasq of dates for each needy person." I said, "Messenger of Allah, by Allah, he does not have even that." The Messenger of Allah said, "I will give him an 'arq (a basket of sixty sa') of dates." I said, "Messenger of Allah, I will give it on his behalf as well." Upon this the Messenger of Allah said, "You have acted rightly and well. Go and give charity on his behalf, and then treat your paternal cousin well." She said, "I did so." (This narration has been cited by Imam Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Talaq.)

These were the circumstances in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and this woman conversed, and concerning this, a command came from above the seven heavens, so that this woman might be given her right, and the hearts of her and her husband might be put at ease, and a principle might be established for the Muslims in matters of this kind, matters of everyday life.

These are the circumstances with which the beginning of a Surah of the Qur'an opens. The Qur'an is an eternal and everlasting Book of Allah, and its significance is that with each single word of it the whole universe keeps pace. The Surah begins thus:

﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband⦆ — Allah is attentive even to the affairs of an ordinary woman among the Muslims. The management of this vast, boundless universe has not occupied Allah away from these affairs, nor has any great matter kept Him from it.

It is a very significant matter that Allah should intervene in such a small, everyday matter, so that the entire Muslim community may realise that Allah is with them, in their circumstances and their affairs, in any great matter or small matter, in everyday matters or in lasting and great issues and problems. Yet Allah is very great, exalted, of supreme dignity, the Compeller and the Proud. All the heavens and the earth belong to Him, and He is Self-Sufficient and, in His own Being, Praiseworthy.

Ḥaḍrat ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: Praise belongs to the One who hears all voices. The woman who argued with the Messenger of Allah was named Khawlah. She came and was in a corner of the house speaking with the Messenger of Allah, and I could not hear her words. Then Allah revealed this verse:

﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah⦆ (Bukhari)

In the narration of Khuwaylah (the name Khuwaylah being used as a diminutive, for endearment or belittlement), the incident, the woman's action, her reaching the Messenger of Allah, her arguing, and the revelation of the Qur'an together present a picture of the life of that unique society in human history. It was a remarkable age: people's connection with the higher world was direct. In every matter of their lives they awaited the guidance of Allah. It was as though all people were the dependants of Allah. People's eyes were fixed on the higher world in the way a child constantly looks towards its mother and father.

The lesson drawn from the narrative of this incident in the Qur'an is that guidance and training were continuously coming from the higher world, and alongside them legislation was also taking place. The Qur'an was framing law in accordance with its own style. This was not dry legislation.

﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your dialogue. Indeed Allah is Hearing and Seeing.﴾ This is a most effective opening. Look, you two who are conversing are not alone; Allah is present with you. He is hearing. He has heard the woman's speech, her complaint about her husband and her plea to Allah. Allah knows everything; He sees and hears. These were the circumstances of that incident, in which Allah was the third party to both of them... all these matters are like pinches and plucks upon the strings of the heart.

And after this, the actual issue is taken up:

The verse in question (58:2) and the commentary on it:

"Those among you who divorce their wives by zihar, saying that their wives are their mothers, their wives are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them. They utter a word that is hateful and false, and surely Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving."

The matter was resolved in great depth. The law of zihar prevalent in the Age of Ignorance (Jahiliyyah) was utterly baseless: a wife does not become a mother, so as to be made unlawful like a mother. A mother is only she who gave birth. By merely uttering a word, a wife does not become a mother and become unlawful. This is an extremely hateful expression. Reality denies it. Truth denies it. Therefore, it is appropriate that social dealings be clear and defined, not ambiguous, unstable and complicated, and that past dealings and incidents have been pardoned by Allah.

"Surely Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving" (58:2). After giving the decision regarding the main issue, now legislation is made thus:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 58, verse 3:

﴿Those who divorce [or rather, declare their wives unlawful, zihar] from among you, then wish to go back on what they said, [the penalty is] the freeing of a slave before the two touch each other. This is what you are admonished to do, and Allah is Aware of what you do.﴾ (58:3)

Allah the Exalted has prescribed the freeing of a slave in several expiations. This was a measure adopted by Islam to end slavery in the world, because in that era the international laws of war permitted slavery. Islam nonetheless adopted various measures to bring about its abolition. Here is the verse:

﴿Then they wish to go back on what they said﴾. There are many opinions regarding the meaning of "then they wish to go back on what they said." It is said that it means they resolve to resume intercourse with the wife, which they had made unlawful upon themselves through zihar. This meaning is closer to the context of the discourse. Therefore, the freeing of a slave is to take place before that intercourse. Regarding this, the admonition:

﴿This is what you are admonished to do﴾. The expiation is a kind of reminder and a lash of warning, so that you do not repeat this act, for this custom is neither right nor a recognized way.

﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾. Allah knows its reality. He is aware of the events and He is aware of your social conduct.

This admonition and lesson came before the completion of the law of zihar, for the training of souls, and because what Allah is legislating, He is legislating in accordance with His knowledge and His wisdom. He is aware of the outward and of the inward. Now, after this, the ruling is completed.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 58, verse 4:

فمن لم ................ مسکینا (85 : 4) "And whoever does not find [a slave], then let him fast two consecutive months before the two touch each other. And whoever is not able to do so, then let him feed sixty needy persons."

Now comes the explanatory statement of this law and the commentary guiding the Muslims.

ذلک لتومنو باللہ ورسولہ (85 : 4) "This ruling is given so that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger." They are already believers, so what is the purpose? The point is that linking these expiations, penalties and their circumstances with the commands and laws of Allah strengthens and increases faith. Practical life is bound up with faith, and faith comes to exercise control over practical life.

وتلک ........................ الیم (85 : 4) "These are the limits set by Allah, and for the disbelievers there is a painful punishment." These limits have been established by Allah so that people do not transgress beyond them. Whoever does not heed them, and does not remain content within them, becomes deserving of His wrath.

وللکفرین عذاب الیم (85 : 4) "And for the disbelievers there is a painful punishment." Because they commit injustice, challenge Allah, do not believe, and do not observe the limits of Allah, as the believers do.

This final statement, وللکفرین عذاب الیم (85 : 4) "And for the disbelievers there is a painful punishment," is in harmony with the conclusion of the preceding verse, and it also establishes the connection with the following verse. Its subject is that those who oppose Allah and His Messenger will be humiliated.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 58, verses 5–6:

In the first paragraph it was explained how very merciful Allah is to the people of Islam, and how He is always ready to resolve the problems of the Muslim community. This second paragraph is for the suppression of the disbelievers: for those who have risen up in enmity against Allah and His Messenger, that is, who adopt opposing and hostile positions regarding the limits (hudud) of the Muslims and engage in confrontation. Since the limits of Allah were mentioned earlier, and whoever disputes over limits is an enemy, that is, whoever fights at the borders, therefore the enemies of Islam are mentioned here, those who stand at the border facing the Messenger of Allah and are making preparations for confrontation. Through this, a picture is given of two opposing parties who fight over the limits. The purpose is to express the ugliness and repulsiveness of the disbelievers' act, because they have come out to fight their Creator and Provider, and they have gathered their satanic armies on the limits of Allah.

﴿Those who oppose Allah and His Messenger will be humiliated, just as those before them were humiliated.﴾ (58:5) The preferred view is that this is a curse upon such people, and a curse from Allah is in reality a divine decree, because Allah "does whatever He wills" (fa'alun lima yurid). Kabt (kabt) means to have wrath descend and to be humiliated. By "those before them" is meant either those who have passed away, the communities of earlier prophets, whom Allah seized for the same crime, or the polytheists and Jews who were humiliated by the Muslims before the revelation of these verses, for example at the Battle of Badr.

﴿And We have sent down clear signs.﴾ (58:5) In this verse, the end of those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, both in this world and in the Hereafter, is described in detail and separately. This is because those who reach this end, described in these verses, do not reach it due to ignorance, nor do they reach it because the matter did not become clear to them. Rather, the matter was explained to them with great clarity. After this, their final end in the Hereafter is presented in a manner that is highly instructive, so that the believers may be reformed and trained.

﴿And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment. On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allah has enumerated it while they forgot it, and Allah is Witness over all things.﴾ (58:6)

Here, a humiliating punishment will be given to them in return for their arrogance. When Allah raises the people, He will inflict a humiliating punishment upon these so-called great ones before the public. This is the punishment that will be given in the presence of truth. Their detailed record of deeds will be behind them, which they will carelessly forget on that Day, although Allah will have prepared it in such a way that nothing from it will remain, because Allah knows everything.

﴿And Allah is Witness over all things.﴾ (58:6)

Here the pictures of mercy, grace, bounty, war, and retribution stand face to face. Allah's knowledge and presence are everywhere. He is present for support, aid and kindness, and He is also present for war, retribution, and punishing the enemies. Therefore, let the believers be reassured by Allah's presence and nearness, and let the disbelievers and enemies be frightened.

That Allah is a witness over all things. Now a living picture of this is presented here. It is so effective that a state of agitation is created in the strings of heart and consciousness.

That Allah is a witness over all things. Now a living picture of this is presented here. It is so effective that a state of agitation is created in the strings of heart and consciousness.

The passage begins with the statement that Allah's knowledge encompasses this universe completely and includes everything. Human thought cannot reach everything within this whole universe, in the far reaches of the heavens and around the earth, whether small or large, apparent or hidden, known or unknown, while everything is within Allah's knowledge. This verse carries human thought out to such distances.

After this, our thought reaches the hearts of those being addressed. Every person's heart is a storehouse of thoughts. Then it is carried to the most secret consultations of people, whether two, three, four, five, or more or less, wherever they are and in whatever gathering they may be.

﴿Never is there a private conversation among three but that He is their fourth, nor among five but that He is their sixth, nor less than that or more but that He is with them wherever they are.﴾ (58:7)

This is a fact in itself, but the beautiful words in which it is expressed make it far more impactful, in a manner that at times makes a person's heart tremble and at other times gives them complete reassurance that Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, is also present with us. Whenever three individuals separate to speak, immediately the awareness will come alive within them that Allah is the fourth among us, and whenever five gather, they will feel that the sixth is Allah. In short, whether there are two or more, Allah is present.

This is a situation before which the human heart cannot stand; it trembles. It is true that for the believers this is a familiar matter, not a strange one, because the belief of the people of faith is that Allah is present and watching. Yet this scene is also extremely frightening.

﴿He is with them wherever they are.﴾ (58:7)

﴿Then He will inform them on the Day of Resurrection of what they did.﴾ (58:7) This is a second, shaking jolt. That Allah is merely present and hears all matters is itself a frightening thing, but that these matters will later be accounted for is even more terrifying, especially in circumstances where the purpose of those who hold secret counsel is that their conspiracy remain hidden. On the Day of Resurrection, the deeds of this secret counsel will be presented in an open court, and all people will be present there, for that is the Day of Witnessing.

Now the conclusion also falls upon the same point with which the beginning was made.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ (58:7) Thus the reality and comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge is planted in hearts. In this one verse, this task is accomplished through various styles, and these styles make this reality deeply rooted in hearts, establishing this same matter within the heart through different paths and doors.

The reality that Allah is present and watching, and which the aforementioned verses establish in hearts in an extremely frightening manner, is in fact brought as a preface for giving the hypocrites a severe warning. These hypocrites used to hold secret counsel constantly against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslim community, and would prepare conspiracies. They were numerous in Madinah. Along with the warning, it is also explained that their position is very strange.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 58, verse 8:

(85 : 8) ﴿Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret counsel, yet they return to that which they were forbidden, and they hold secret counsels together in sin, enmity, and disobedience to the Messenger? When they come to you, they greet you with a greeting with which Allah has not greeted you, and they say within themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?" Hell is sufficient for them; they will burn in it, and wretched is the destination.﴾

This verse shows that in Madinah the Prophet's (ﷺ) approach toward the hypocrites (munafiqun) was extremely tolerant and compassionate. He advised them to accept Islam sincerely, and he repeatedly forbade them from secret counsel (najwa), conspiracies, and covert plotting. The hypocrites carried out this work together with the Jews. Indeed, all of these activities were carried out by the polytheists and the hypocrites at the instigation of the Jews. Despite the Prophet's (ﷺ) sincere conduct, they intensified their conspiracies, covert schemes, and secret counsels. They also began to adopt means and strategies aimed at disobeying the Prophet's (ﷺ) commands, and at creating mischief in the affairs of the Muslims and in the Islamic order in order to disrupt them.

These people became so bold and daring in their activities that, alongside interfering with the orders of the Islamic state, they also created mischief in the greeting exchanged with the Prophet (ﷺ). They had even altered the meaning of as-salamu alaykum.

﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with a greeting with which Allah has not greeted you﴾. These hypocrites and Jews would say as-sam alaykum instead of as-salamu alaykum, meaning "may death come upon you." Likewise, they had fabricated some other expressions whose outward form was good but whose inner meaning they used in a wrong sense. They would then say that if this man were truly a Prophet, he would know about our words, or about the gatherings in which we plan measures and conspiracies against him.

This surah shows that Allah had informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of everything. He knew both what they thought in their hearts and the conspiracies they carried out in their gatherings. At the beginning of the surah it was made clear that Allah heard the words of the woman who was disputing with the Prophet (ﷺ) about her husband. It was also stated that if three people hold secret counsel, the fourth is Allah, and if four do so, the fifth is Allah, and that He knows whatever is within their souls. After this, their claims were refuted.

﴿Hell is sufficient for them; they will burn in it, and wretched is the destination.﴾

The exposure of their secret plots, and especially of their secret counsels carried out despite the Prophet's (ﷺ) prohibition, and the exposure of what they said in their hearts, that if this is a true Prophet then he should know of these schemes, all these disclosures are proof that Allah knows every matter of the heavens and the earth. Allah is present in every secret consultation, and He is the witness of every private gathering. All these matters were frightening for the hypocrites, since all their affairs had been exposed, while for the believers they became a source of reassurance and trust.

Now the address turns to the believers: "O you who have believed, do not hold secret counsel as the hypocrites do, in matters of sin, enmity, and disobedience to the Messenger. Rather, whatever you say, say it with fear of Allah. This kind of secret counsel is in fact inspired by Satan, and through it Satan wants to distress the believers. Yet such secret counsel is not becoming of the believers."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 58, verses 9–10:

"O you who have believed, when you confer privately, do not confer in sin and transgression and disobedience to the Messenger, but confer in righteousness and piety. And fear Allah, to whom you will be returned (gathered). Secret conferring is only from Satan, so that he may grieve those who believe, but it will not harm them at all, except by Allah's permission. And upon Allah let the believers rely." (58:9–10)

It appears that in the early period, when people had not yet developed a proper awareness and sentiment of the Islamic community, some Muslims would begin collective consultation among themselves in collective matters without consulting their leadership. These people were not yet acquainted with the spirit of Islamic organization, according to which every consultation or proposal should first come before the leadership, and there should be no secret counsel outside Islamic leadership. It appears that in that era, some Muslims, owing to their inexperience, when they held such consultations, complications arose from them, and the Muslim community was troubled by them, even though those consulting did not have such an intention. Yet merely raising such issues by these people would become a cause of harm to the community, and would result in disobedience of the collective policy.

This is why the people of faith are addressed with the title of faith, which provides the foundation of their new collective identity.

"O you who have believed" (58:9): Do not hold consultations that involve sins and transgress limits, and that entail disobedience to the Messenger ﷺ. And it is also explained on what matters the people of faith may consult.

"But confer in righteousness and piety" (58:9): You may certainly consult about adopting means and measures for righteousness and piety. Al-Birr: that is, general good; al-Taqwa: vigilance and fear of Allah, considering Him as witnessing and present. This kind of piety teaches only goodness. Then it is explicitly said to them: fear Allah, to whom you will return. There He will call you to account for all that you have done. He is the one who prepares this complete record and will also be a witness to it, however much you may conceal and keep hidden.

Imam Ahmad narrated through Bahz and Affan, from Hammam, from Qatadah, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, who said: I was holding the hand of Ibn Umar when a man asked him: "What did you hear from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about najwa (secret counsel) and what will happen concerning it on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah will draw near to a believer and place His hands upon him, so that he will be hidden from the people. He will make him acknowledge his sins and say: You know such-and-such sin? Until, when He has reminded him of all his sins and he has acknowledged them, and that person thinks that he is ruined, Allah will say: Indeed, in the world I concealed these sins for you, and today I forgive you all of them. Then Allah will give him the record of his good deeds. As for the disbelievers and hypocrites, the witnesses present will say: These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Curse be upon the wrongdoers." (Bukhari)

After this, believers are forbidden from secret counsel, spreading rumours, and covert plots. No one should hold private consultations apart from the community, because the believers are part of this community; their interest and the interest of the community are one. They should not separate from the community in any matter. And they are told that when believers see some people whispering apart and holding separate consultations, this will cause the believers doubt, anxiety and grief, and an atmosphere of mistrust will arise. Satan's very scheme is to incite those who engage in such secret counsel, so that by conferring they trouble the Muslim community, although he cannot cause them any harm.

"Secret conferring is only from Satan, so that he may grieve those who believe, but it will not harm them at all, except by Allah's permission, and upon Allah let the believers rely" (58:10): No believer relies on anyone other than Allah, for reliance can be placed on none but Allah, and there is no other being such.

It comes in the Hadith that in such circumstances one should not engage in whispering which creates doubts and suspicions, damages the mutual trust of Muslims, and generates fears in hearts.

Abd Allah ibn Masud (may Allah be pleased with him) narrates: "If two of you should not consult apart from a third, because that would grieve him." These are the best manners of the Islamic community. If such manners are observed, there will be no room left for doubts and suspicions. Yes, if there is a wisdom in keeping a matter confidential, or the concealment of someone is desired, or the matter concerns a particular person, or concealment is desired in a general discussion, then there is no prohibition against speaking in a closed room. Such a situation usually occurs among the leaders of the community. But no gathering should be such that it could be called a community within a community, or one that happens without the knowledge of the community. The Qur'an and Sunnah have prohibited this kind of najwa, and such secret counsel produces division within communities and doubts within their ranks; this is the disease which Satan spreads with great care, so that he may spread dissatisfaction among the people of faith. Here Allah has decided that He will never let the Muslim community come to harm, because Allah Himself is the overseer, guardian and protector of the community of believers, and Allah is present in every secret counsel. And in such consultations, whatever plots are made, Allah renders them harmless to the believers.

"Except by Allah's permission" (58:10): Wherever there is a definite and firm promise or decision, this kind of exception occurs; its purpose is that Allah is not Himself bound by His decisions. Therefore Allah does whatever He wills; if Allah wills that the Muslims be troubled, He can do so.

"And upon Allah let the believers rely" (58:10): Allah is the one who saves and supports. He is the Mighty and the Dear, He is the All-Knowing and All-Aware, He is the Witness and the Present, and in this universe only that happens which Allah wills. And since Allah has promised that He will save the believers, what doubt remains for the believers after this? Therefore they become free of worry.

After this, the people of faith are taught another collective etiquette.

Yet merely raising such issues by these people would become a cause of harm to the community, and would result in disobedience of the collective policy.

"O you who have believed" (58:9): Do not hold consultations that involve sins and transgress limits, and that entail disobedience to the Messenger ﷺ. And it is also explained on what matters the people of faith may consult.

"But confer in righteousness and piety" (58:9): You may certainly consult about adopting means and measures for righteousness and piety. Al-Birr: that is, general good; al-Taqwa: vigilance and fear of Allah, considering Him as witnessing and present. This kind of piety teaches only goodness. Then it is explicitly said to them: fear Allah, to whom you will return. There He will call you to account for all that you have done. He is the one who prepares this complete record and will also be a witness to it, however much you may conceal and keep hidden.

Imam Ahmad narrated through Bahz and Affan, from Hammam, from Qatadah, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, who said: I was holding the hand of Ibn Umar when a man asked him: "What did you hear from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about najwa (secret counsel) and what will happen concerning it on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah will draw near to a believer and place His hands upon him, so that he will be hidden from the people. He will make him acknowledge his sins and say: You know such-and-such sin? Until, when He has reminded him of all his sins and he has acknowledged them, and that person thinks that he is ruined, Allah will say: Indeed, in the world I concealed these sins for you, and today I forgive you all of them. Then Allah will give him the record of his good deeds. As for the disbelievers and hypocrites, the witnesses present will say: These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Curse be upon the wrongdoers." (Bukhari)

After this, believers are forbidden from secret counsel, spreading rumours, and covert plots. No one should hold private consultations apart from the community, because the believers are part of this community; their interest and the interest of the community are one. They should not separate from the community in any matter. And they are told that when believers see some people whispering apart and holding separate consultations, this will cause the believers doubt, anxiety and grief, and an atmosphere of mistrust will arise. Satan's very scheme is to incite those who engage in such secret counsel, so that by conferring they trouble the Muslim community, although he cannot cause them any harm.

"Secret conferring is only from Satan, so that he may grieve those who believe, but it will not harm them at all, except by Allah's permission, and upon Allah let the believers rely" (58:10): No believer relies on anyone other than Allah, for reliance can be placed on none but Allah, and there is no other being such.

It comes in the Hadith that in such circumstances one should not engage in whispering which creates doubts and suspicions, damages the mutual trust of Muslims, and generates fears in hearts.

Abd Allah ibn Masud (may Allah be pleased with him) narrates: "If two of you should not consult apart from a third, because that would grieve him." These are the best manners of the Islamic community. If such manners are observed, there will be no room left for doubts and suspicions. Yes, if there is a wisdom in keeping a matter confidential, or the concealment of someone is desired, or the matter concerns a particular person, or concealment is desired in a general discussion, then there is no prohibition against speaking in a closed room. Such a situation usually occurs among the leaders of the community. But no gathering should be such that it could be called a community within a community, or one that happens without the knowledge of the community. The Qur'an and Sunnah have prohibited this kind of najwa, and such secret counsel produces division within communities and doubts within their ranks; this is the disease which Satan spreads with great care, so that he may spread dissatisfaction among the people of faith. Here Allah has decided that He will never let the Muslim community come to harm, because Allah Himself is the overseer, guardian and protector of the community of believers, and Allah is present in every secret counsel. And in such consultations, whatever plots are made, Allah renders them harmless to the believers.

"Except by Allah's permission" (58:10): Wherever there is a definite and firm promise or decision, this kind of exception occurs; its purpose is that Allah is not Himself bound by His decisions. Therefore Allah does whatever He wills; if Allah wills that the Muslims be troubled, He can do so.

"And upon Allah let the believers rely" (58:10): Allah is the one who saves and supports. He is the Mighty and the Dear, He is the All-Knowing and All-Aware, He is the Witness and the Present, and in this universe only that happens which Allah wills. And since Allah has promised that He will save the believers, what doubt remains for the believers after this? Therefore they become free of worry.

After this, the people of faith are taught another collective etiquette.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 58, verse 11:

Some narrations indicate that the revelation of these verses is also connected with the hypocrites (munafiqin). Through them, the connection between these verses and the preceding verses becomes clear. Qatadah says that these verses were revealed concerning gatherings of remembrance (majalis-i-dhikr). The attitude of the hypocrites was that when they saw a person coming to the assembly of the Messenger, they would sit firmly in their places. Therefore Allah commanded that newcomers be given room in the assembly.

Miqatil ibn Hayyan said that it was revealed concerning Friday. On that day the Prophet (ﷺ) was in the Suffah, and the space was cramped. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to honour greatly those from among the Muhajirun and Ansar who were people of Badr. Some people of Badr came, and the space before them had already been filled. They stood around the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said:

"As-salamu alaykum ayyuha al-Nabi wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh." The Prophet (ﷺ) returned the greeting. After that they greeted those sitting there, and they too returned the greeting. These people kept standing, perhaps those people would create space in the assembly for them. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) found out why they were standing. This matter was very displeasing to the Prophet (ﷺ). So, among the Muhajirun and Ansar around him, those who were not from Badr, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "So-and-so, you get up; so-and-so, you get up." In this way the Prophet (ﷺ) kept raising them until there was room for all the people of Badr to sit. This matter was very burdensome to those who were made to rise. The Prophet (ﷺ) saw this aversion on their faces. Upon this, the hypocrites said: "Do you not believe that your 'companion' is just among the people?" So they said: "To us, such raising does not seem to be just." Some people sought closeness to the Prophet and sat close, and he raised them and then remained sitting for a long time. It reached us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on the one who made room in the assembly for his brother." After that, if someone came, those people would quickly rise to give them room. People began to make room for one another in the assemblies, and this verse was revealed on the day of Friday.

If this narration is authentic, it is not contrary to those ahadith which state that a person should not be raised from an assembly so that another may sit in his place. As in the narration in the Sahihayn: "No one should raise another person from a gathering in order that he himself may sit in that place, but rather make room and create spaciousness in the assemblies." And it is likewise not contrary to other ahadith whose content is that the latecomer should sit where the assembly ends, and should not climb over the necks of people to advance so that he may sit in a prominent place.

The meaning of the verse is that those already seated should make room for the one who comes. Just as the verse also says that if the organisers tell someone to vacate his seat, he should vacate it. But this command must come from the organiser and leadership, not from the one coming from outside.

The point here is that spaciousness must be created in human souls before spaciousness is created in assemblies. If spaciousness arises in the heart, then it will bear with others, and will seat brothers coming into the assembly with the utmost love and the utmost good manners, will welcome them, and will make room for them with great joy and willingness.

But if the leadership considers that, because of some particular matter or special circumstances, it is necessary to vacate a place, then one should vacate it with a contented heart and gladly. Yet the principle remains the same: the one who comes later should remain behind, and should not advance by riding over people's necks, nor raise someone else in order to sit in his place. This is tolerance and an administrative command, which is decisive, and Islam in any case teaches the finest manners.

After every command, the principle of the Islamic system of training is that it reforms the consciousness of people. Here too it is said that if you create spaciousness in assemblies and in hearts, Allah will create spaciousness for you.

"Fafsahu ... lakum" (58:11): "So make room, Allah will make room for you." And those who give up their places and obey the Messenger or the leadership, Allah will grant them elevated rank.

"Wa idha qila ... darajat" (58:11): "And when you are told to rise, then rise. Allah will raise to high ranks those among you who believe and who have been given knowledge." This is the reward of their humility and the recompense of obeying the command and discipline.

Seeking a near position in the assembly of the Prophet (ﷺ) was in essence for the sake of acquiring knowledge. Therefore this verse teaches them that the faith which teaches spaciousness of heart, teaches obedience to command, and the knowledge which grants refinement of the heart, and when the heart becomes spacious and obedient, then the ranks of such knowledge and of the one who seeks it are raised high with Allah. And this rank that was granted was granted because they, following the Messenger's command, gave up their place in the assembly. Therefore Allah gave them a rank in His presence.

"Wallahu ... khabir" (58:11): "And Allah is aware of what you do." Therefore Allah will give a fitting reward for every deed on the basis of knowledge and understanding, and Allah also knows what motive lies behind your actions.

Thus the Noble Qur'an refines human souls and morally trains them, and teaches people spaciousness of heart, tolerance, and obedience to command, so that they perform even disagreeable acts with zeal and willingness. The religion of Islam is not merely a law consisting of dry clauses. It is a consciousness, an outlook, a sentiment, and a faculty within the conscience that urges one to action.

Now the Noble Qur'an teaches the believers another etiquette concerning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

It appears that those who conversed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) privately had become very numerous, and every individual wanted to converse with the Prophet (ﷺ) about his personal affairs and sought guidance and counsel in his private matters. In that period the collective responsibilities of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had increased, and his time was very precious. Private conversation with him had become a very important and serious matter. This could only be for some extremely important issue, yet people were rushing forward for this honour. Therefore, in order to control those who demanded private time, Allah imposed a financial penalty. And this financial penalty was for the collective works of the community. Thus the Prophet (ﷺ) would give a portion of his time to such people, since his entire time was dedicated to collective affairs. This penalty was that whoever wished to have private time would first give charity.

O you who believe, when you consult the Messenger privately, ﴿spend something in charity before your private consultation. That is better for you and purer. But if you cannot find anything, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (85:21)

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) acted upon this verse. He had a dinar, which he exchanged for silver coins (dirhams). Whenever he consulted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) privately, he would give one dirham in charity. But this ruling was very burdensome for the Muslims. Allah already knew. The purpose behind this command had been fulfilled. People had come to know how precious the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was. Therefore Allah withdrew this command, and the next verse came down.

And it directed them toward worship and obedience to Allah.

﴿Are you afraid that before your private conference you will have to give charity? So if you do not do this, and Allah has forgiven you, then keep establishing prayer, keep giving zakah, and keep obeying Allah and His Messenger. Allah is well aware of what you do.﴾ (85 : 31)

From the philosophy of these two verses and the hadiths narrated about their revelation, it becomes clear how much effort was made to train the Muslims in matters both small and great, and to prepare the Islamic community.

Now the context turns back to the hypocrites. These people had deep friendship and close relations with the Jews. Some of their circumstances are laid bare, and they are warned that all their deeds are no longer hidden, and that their end will be very bad. Despite all your conspiracies, the Islamic call is now advancing on the path to success.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 58, verse 14:

This is a critical attack on the hypocrites (munafiqeen). It is said that these people are forming friendships with a people upon whom Allah has brought His wrath. From this it is understood that these hypocrites used to devise extremely deep plots against the Muslims, and they used to prepare these conspiracies together with the fiercest enemies of the Muslims, namely the Jews. Further, from this it is also understood that the authority of Islam had become firmly established. Because when the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims criticized them and called them to account, these people used to swear false oaths. Whereas what the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims said was based on the revelations provided by Allah. When they took oaths, they knew well that they were liars. They used their oaths as a shield to protect themselves from this accountability, because all their conspiracies were liable to be held accountable by the Islamic state.

﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾ (al-Mujadila 58:16; Qur'an 58:16 as quoted in the original: 63:2) "They have made their oaths a shield." In this way they continue their conspiracies and keep people away from the path of Allah.

In between these verses, Allah repeatedly warned them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 58, verses 15–16:

"﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment .................... evil indeed are the deeds they have been doing﴾" (85 : 51). And what follows is:

"﴿So for them ........ a humiliating punishment﴾" (85 : 61). What follows is:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 58, verses 15–16:

"﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment .................... evil indeed are the deeds they have been doing﴾" (85 : 51). And what follows is:

"﴿So for them ........ a humiliating punishment﴾" (85 : 61). What follows is:

﴿Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them against Allah in any way. They are the companions of the Fire, and therein they will abide forever.﴾ (85 : 71)

The picture drawn in these verses of their condition on the Day of Resurrection is very crude and demeaning. Just as they swear false oaths in the world, so too they are seen swearing oaths before Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 58, verses 18–19:

On the day when Allah raises them all up, they will swear to Him just as they swear to you, and they will think that they have something to stand on. Surely they are the liars.

This shows that hypocrisy has become ingrained in their very nature. Even on the Day of Resurrection it will remain with them, and they will dare to tell false oaths before Allah, the Lord of Majesty, even though at that time they will know that Allah knows what is in the hearts.

﴿And they will think that they have something to stand on.﴾ They will think that this will benefit them. Yet they are hanging in the air, with no earth beneath their feet... They are genuine liars.

﴿Indeed, they are the liars.﴾

The cause of these actions is that Satan has completely overpowered them.

﴿So he made them forget the remembrance of Allah﴾ (58:19). He has caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah from their hearts. And a heart that forgets Allah becomes corrupt and becomes purely devoted to evil.

﴿Those are the party of Satan﴾ (58:19). The party of Satan works purely for him, marches under his banner, acts in his name, and fulfils his aims. This party is pure evil, and it will be purely in loss.

﴿Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers.﴾ This is a very severe and harsh critical assault against these hypocrites. This extended critical assault was made because they were engaged day and night in extremely dangerous conspiracies, constantly plotting measures against the Muslims in league with the Jews. From this critical assault it is evident that the Muslims must have been greatly reassured, and will continue to be, that Allah Himself is devising measures on their behalf.

These hypocrites sought refuge with the Jews and believed that the Jews were a formidable power, feared by people, and that hopes were also tied to them. For this reason they sought counsel and support from them. Therefore Allah disappoints them regarding the Jews and says that humiliation and defeat have been decreed upon those Jews. And Allah is Mighty, and His Messenger will also remain victorious.

ان الذین ........................ قوی عزیز (12) (85 : 02۔ 12) "Surely those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are among the most humiliated of creatures. Allah has decreed: 'I and My Messengers will surely prevail.' Indeed, Allah is All-Powerful and Mighty."

This is the true promise of Allah, which has been fulfilled and will continue to be fulfilled, even if the circumstances of this true promise may appear to be contrary.

In practice, what happened in Jazirat al-Arab (the Arabian Peninsula) was exactly this: Iman (faith) and Tawhid (Divine oneness) prevailed. Kufr (disbelief) and Shirk (associating partners with Allah) were overcome, and the Islamic way of life became dominant in Jazirat al-Arab. After a long struggle against Kufr and Shirk, and after removing the obstacles, the whole of humanity bowed before the belief in Tawhid. Although, in some regions of the world, Shirk and Kufr have gained dominance for a temporary period, just as today Shirk-based beliefs are dominant in some places under atheist and idol-worshipping governments, the belief in Tawhid has remained dominant throughout the world. Moreover, Ilhad (atheism) and Shirk are continuously in decline, because Shirk, in its various manifestations, is not fit to remain in the world. Modern science has also provided humanity with many modern arguments for the belief in Tawhid, so Iman and Tawhid are continuously progressing, and Shirk-based beliefs and ideologies are shrinking.

A believer regards Allah's promise as a reality. If, at any time, a limited generation or a limited piece of land appears to be against it, he should be certain that this situation is temporary and will change. This temporary dominance of Kufr also occurs under some wisdom, and perhaps it is so that the People of Faith may see it as a challenge to their faith-based honour, and rise up against it, so that it may be overcome in accordance with Allah's promise.

In our present age, the enemies of faith are at war with the People of Faith from every side, and they are attacking from every direction. They have begun an unending war against faith. From every side, there is persecution, conspiracy, and continuous and varied plotting against Islam and Iman. Muslims are being killed, expelled from their homelands, subjected to all kinds of torture, deprived of their means of livelihood, and every kind of humiliation has been imposed upon them. Despite all this, the hearts of the People of Faith are full of faith. They are protected from falling, and they do not melt and merge into the dominant nations. Even while enduring these difficulties, they are waiting for opportunities to attack Kufr and shatter it to pieces. For a long time, Muslims have been facing this situation, but their faith is firm, and they are engaged in struggle. This shows that Allah and His Messenger will surely prevail, and in this matter they will not have to wait a long time.

Therefore, the believer should not entertain any doubt in his heart that faith will remain dominant. Allah's promise is a reality, and sooner or later it will take the form of reality. Those who are enemies of Allah, the Messenger of Allah, and Islam will be humiliated, and Allah and His Messenger will remain dominant. This is how it happens, and it will happen. But apparently, circumstances are such that they appear to be against it.

And finally, the principle upon which Muslims should firmly stand: this is the fundamental principle, and it is a scale for the truthfulness of faith and for false claims of faith.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran) on Surah 58, verse 22:

"You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kindred. These are the ones in whose hearts Allah has written faith and whom He has strengthened with a spirit from Himself. He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. They are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah are the successful ones."

This is a complete separation between the party of Allah (ḥizb Allāh) and the party of Satan (ḥizb al-Shayṭān). Leaving aside all ties and all attractions, the community of Muslims should devote itself single-mindedly, and hold firmly together to one rope, the rope of faith.

"You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger." This is because Allah has not placed two hearts within a single person. No human being can hold two loves in his heart; that is, one cannot have love for Allah and His Messenger and also love for the enemies of Allah and His Messenger. Either there is faith, or there is disbelief (kufr). These two cannot be gathered in one heart.

"Even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kindred." When the boundaries of faith begin, the ties of blood and kinship are severed. If there is no conflict between the two banners, then ties of blood and kinship may be maintained. The two banners here mean the banner of Allah and the banner of Satan. If there is no war between the party of Allah and the party of Satan, and parents and relatives are not supporters of the party of Satan in the state of war, then the Sharia permits good relations with parents and relatives. But if enmity, opposition and hostility continue, then Islam commands that all ties be cut, and that one hold fast only to the one firm rope, the rope of faith. Abu 'Ubaydah killed his father on the day of Badr. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) had resolved to kill his son 'Abd al-Rahman. Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr killed his brother 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr. 'Umar, Hamzah, 'Ali, 'Ubaydah and al-Harith killed their close relatives and members of their clans. They did not regard blood and kinship at all, and gave importance to the faith and the ideology. This was the high standard to which Islam raised ideological ties.

"These are the ones in whose hearts Allah has written faith." Allah has firmly established faith in their hearts. The Most Merciful wrote it in their hearts with His own hand, so it can neither be erased from their hearts nor face decline; it cannot be extinguished, nor can any complexity arise within it.

"And has strengthened them with a spirit from Himself." The resolve they have made to follow the path of faith and to bring about the Islamic revolution, they have done through this spiritual strength, and their souls have been illumined by this strength of radiance and divine support. This very spirit connects them to the true source of that light and radiance.

"He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever." This is the reward for their having become sincere for Allah, for having founded their relations solely upon the bond of faith, and for having cast aside all the aims and all the enmities of this transient world.

"Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him." This is a most luminous, beautiful, contented and tranquil picture, through which a true believer is placed at a very exalted station: the very pleasing and affectionate image that their Lord is pleased with them and they are pleased with their Lord. Cutting themselves off from the whole world, they have become with Allah, and Allah has taken them under His protection. He has prepared for them vast gardens and has informed them that He is pleased with them; therefore, through this closeness, they too have attained intimacy and tranquillity.

"They are the party of Allah." They are the party of Allah. They have gathered under the banner of Allah; they are assembled under the leadership of Allah. They proceed in accordance with Allah's guidance and wish to establish His system. The hand of Allah's power works through them, and they are the decree of Allah.

"Unquestionably, the party of Allah are the successful ones." The question is: if the helper of Allah does not attain success, then who else will attain it? Thus all humanity is divided into two parties: the party of Allah and the party of Satan. There are only two banners: the banner of Allah and the banner of Satan. Whoever is in the party of Allah will be under the banner of Allah, and whoever is under the banner of Satan will be in the party of Satan, and will be a follower of falsehood. These are two opposing qualities and two opposing parties.

There is no lineage, no kinship, no relatives or close relations, no homeland or race that counts. There is no tribalism or nationalism; there is only creed, creed and faith. Whoever inclines to the party of Allah and stands beneath the banners of truth, he and all those who stand beneath that banner are brothers in the way of Allah. They are in different lands, among different peoples and tribes, in different races and clans, yet they are brothers because they are the party of Allah. The party of Allah is a bond under which all distinctions melt away. And whoever has been overcome by Satan and stands under the banner of falsehood is not a brother or relative of any member of the party of Allah: not in land, not in race, not in people, not in colour, not in kinship. Because the first bond among the people of truth has been established, which is the bond of creed; other bonds arise only after it.

From the indications of this verse it is understood that at that time there were people among the Muslims who gave importance to blood, kinship, interests and the ties of friendship. This verse seeks to train such people. Accordingly, this verse commands the establishing of decisive and clear Islamic bonds. Yet this same verse also shows that within the Islamic community there were people who had already severed these worldly ties; they adhered only to Islamic bonds and had fulfilled the goal of Islam.

This is also a fitting conclusion to this surah, which began with the theme that Allah is meeting every need of each member of His community, to the extent that He resolves the affairs even of a very poor and destitute household. A poor woman who was disputing with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and complaining about herself and about her husband: Allah resolved her problems.

Therefore, for this community to be wholly cut off from all other ties and to belong to Allah is a natural matter, which fulfils their smaller needs; it is a natural and appropriate thing. Moreover, for a community which Allah calls His party, and which He has raised up in this universe for a most important role, to be thus severed for Allah is a natural matter.
